category_title: Pre-engaged students with organizational and focus challenges
minimal_context: The student is seated at his desk looking for a decodable booklet to begin a quick read decoding activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to start the quick read decoding activity. Please find your copy of the booklet in your desk.

STUDENT: (Busy digging through his desk as several wrinkled booklets fall out) I'm not sure if I have the right one.

TUTOR: Keep looking to see if you can find it.

STUDENT: (Puts the wrinkled booklets aside and continues digging)

TUTOR: Just do your best to get ready.

STUDENT: (Gets distracted and eventually stuffs all of the booklets back into his desk, missing the quick read entirely)

options.A: Using opportunities to respond (OTRs) to maintain the student's orientation and engagement with the decoding activity.
options.B: Articulating the alternatives the student confronted and the action taken, asking, "How can you change this to a better decision?"
options.C: Terminating the task demand and removing the decodable booklets from the student's desk for 10 seconds.
options.D: Ignoring all undesirable behaviors exhibited by the student as they search for the decodable booklet.
